column2: On the authority of Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until his inclination follows what I have brought.” A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith; we have narrated it in Kitāb al-Ḥujjah with an authentic chain.
Lā yuʾminu (“does not truly believe”): [with] complete faith. Hawāhu (“his inclination”): what his soul loves and inclines to. “Follows what I have brought”: the pure Sharīʿah.
Every legally responsible person must have his inclination follow what Muḥammad ﷺ brought.
Whoever's inclination does not follow what Muḥammad ﷺ brought is either deficient in faith or outside it.
The obligation to love the Messenger ﷺ; and it is a requirement of loving him to follow him in what he commanded and avoid what he forbade.
This hadith teaches us that no person truly believes until he loves what the Messenger ﷺ brought and acts on it, and hates what he forbade and avoids it;

and that he does not do any deed until he measures it against the Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ: if it agrees with the Book and the Sunnah, he does it, and if there is in them what forbids it or rejects it, he avoids it

and turns away from it. This is the reality of one whose inclination follows what Muḥammad ﷺ brought: “And whatever the Messenger has given you, take; and what he has forbidden you, refrain from. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty” [al-Ḥashr 59:7].
And on the opposite of the meaning of this hadith, concerning blameworthy inclination:
When the soul calls you one day to some need, / and there is a way to oppose it,
then oppose its desire as much as you can, for / its desire is an enemy and opposing it a friend.
The bane of the intellect is desire; whoever's intellect / rises above his desire is saved.
Humiliation (hawān) is desire (hawā) with its name shortened; / so when you follow desire, you have met humiliation.
The nūn of hawān (humiliation) is stolen from hawā (desire), / and everyone felled by desire is felled by humiliation.
In the first verse the printed text reads فخاف (“fear”), evidently for فخالف (“oppose”), as in the same verse under hadith 6.
